location.ref: Bhāber Gīt, the songs of the bazaar and the company

paraphrase: The songs speak of a new company come to the bazaar, of merchants, goods and profits: the soul trades in the market of the world, and the true merchandise is the Master's secret, which the wise buy while fools trade in empty goods.
speaker: Dulālcānd
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Thematic summary (gist moderate, detail low), following H. B. Urban's account of the songs' imagery.

location.ref: Bhāber Gīt, on the Master hidden in man

paraphrase: The Master (Kartā) is hidden in the human form, the sahaja mānuṣa; he cannot be found by outward religion, only by the one who has received the secret from the Mahāśay.
speaker: Dulālcānd
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Thematic summary.

location.ref: Bhāber Gīt, on caste in the Kartā's fellowship

paraphrase: In the Kartā's fellowship there is one caste: brahmin and low-caste, Hindu and Muslim sit and eat together as his servants.
speaker: Dulālcānd
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
